title: Survive the AI Knife Fight: Building Products That Win — Brian Balfour, Reforge
talk_summary: Brian Balfour argues that in the AI 'knife fight,' competitive advantage comes not from building models or copying chatbot features, but from assembling off-the-shelf AI capabilities with proprietary data, product functionality, and insight into unmet customer needs. He illustrates with Granola, which used commodity transcription/LLM APIs but differentiated through note-enhancement workflow, Mac-app capture, and a compounding notes repository.

takeaways.technique: Differentiation from proprietary data + functionality, not the model
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats AI models as commodity Lego blocks; builds moat by combining unique data, product functionality, and unmet-need insight into a flywheel.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Your competitive advantage will come from what is uniquely yours. These three things, your data, your functionality, and your understanding of unmet customer needs, not the AI itself.

takeaways.what_they_do: Continuously recombines the initial building blocks into new unique sets rather than stopping at first assembly; each layer buys time to build the next.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The real moat is just a sequence of smaller moes stacked together. Each one buys time.
takeaways.numbers: moat window cited as 2 to 3 weeks today vs 6 to 12 months before
